rationale:
Evidence from iteration 3 (score 338.4, down from 398.1). The s-bend improved a lot: progress rose from 0.42 to 0.74 and 3 of 20 runs finished. The oval got worse: completions fell from 20/20 to 9/20, off-track ends rose to 11, and steering_oscillation rose from 0.14 to 0.23. The slalom barely moved (progress 0.19). So kp 6.0 with kd 1.5 gives useful extra correction on bends but overshoots and oscillates on the gentler oval. Line loss is not the main problem; the off-track limit is 0.06 m.

Changes: (1) kp reduced from 6.0 to 5.0 to cut the overshoot that is hurting the oval, keeping most of the bend gain. (2) kd raised from 1.5 to 1.8 to damp the oscillation at the new kp (kd/kp rises from 0.25 to 0.36). (3) base_speed held at 1.1, since the oval finished in time at 1.1 and lowering it further would cost time and the completion bonus is worth more. (4) Geometry is kept identical to iteration 3 (sensors at y 0.08, x ±0.07, size 0.016, wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.7, body 0.14 by 0.12), so the controller change is isolated. ki stays at 0 and line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: oval completion back above 75 percent with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.2, s-bend progress above 0.6, and slalom progress above 0.25.

Hypotheses: (H1) the oval off-track failures come from overshoot at kp 6, so a kp near 5 restores oval completion while keeping most of the s-bend gain. (H2) the slalom fails because the sensor lead and response are too slow for alternating curves, so it may need a further kp or kd change, or a larger base speed reduction. (H3) wheel_track 0.10 may be adding yaw gain that contributes to oscillation; if the oval stays weak, the next step is to restore wheel_track to 0.12. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, to separate overshoot from lag.
